_about: Shared row definitions for the 'why would a developer use NDTwin' comparison (report ~2026-10-21). Every research worker fills cells for these exact row ids. [Co-developed with claude code -- Adam]

verdicts.builtin: documented feature does the task out of the box (config/flags allowed, no new code)
verdicts.diy: possible, but the developer writes code or bolts on another tool; say what
verdicts.no: not supported or out of the tool's scope
verdicts.unknown: public docs are silent; say where you looked

cell_schema.note: <= 20 words, your own words, no marketing adjectives
cell_schema.source: URL (competitors) or repo path:line on trunk 2ece656c (NDTwin)

app.label: Developer writing a network control app

rows.A1: Read the topology (switches, links, hosts) through an API
rows.A2: List active flows with their path and rate
rows.A3: Read per-link utilization in near real time
rows.A4: Install or change forwarding rules from an external app
rows.A5: Fail a link on purpose and watch the app react
rows.A6: Ask 'what if' before applying a change (simulate the effect)
rows.A7: Run the same app code on OpenFlow and on P4 data planes
rows.A8: Run the same app code on an emulated network and on real switches

rows.P1: Compile and run my own .p4 on a software switch
rows.P2: Get a multi-switch topology with hosts built for me
rows.P3: Write table entries at runtime through an API
rows.P4: Link/topology discovery keeps working with my own P4 program
rows.P5: Per-flow telemetry (who talks to whom, at what rate) without writing my own
rows.P6: Automated packet-level tests generated for my program
rows.P7: Network-wide view (graph or GUI) of my P4 network
rows.P8: Path from software switch to a hardware target

ops.label: Network operator

rows.O1: Mirror a running network's live state (topology, flows, load)
rows.O2: Check configuration correctness (reachability, ACLs) before a change
rows.O3: Predict congestion after removing a link or switch (traffic-aware what-if)
rows.O4: Run real vendor network OS images
rows.O5: Run fault-injection drills on a copy, not on production
rows.O6: Energy-saving analysis (which devices can be powered down)
rows.O7: Turn a natural-language intent into a network action
rows.O8: Record and replay historical network state

competitors: Cisco Modeling Labs (commercial, public docs only)
IRTF NMRG network digital twin architecture draft (academic reference framework)

maturity_rows.M2: Cost to a developer (free / free tier / paid; list price if public)
maturity_rows.M4: GitHub stars (unauthenticated public page/API, give the number and date) or 'not on GitHub'
maturity_rows.M5: Contributors (approx., from the public repo) or 'closed source'
maturity_rows.M6: Fidelity: packet-level emulation / packet-level simulation / flow-level model / config model / ML model
maturity_rows.M7: Largest documented scale (nodes/links/hosts), with the source
maturity_rows.M8: Install path (package, VM image, container, SaaS) and documented prerequisites
maturity_rows.M9: Primary programmatic interface (REST, gRPC/P4Runtime, Python API, CLI, none)
